ACBusType.description: Classification of an AC bus for power flow, following the MATPOWER bus-type convention. `PQ` fixes the active and reactive injections and solves for voltage magnitude and angle; `PV` fixes active power and voltage magnitude and solves for reactive power and angle; `REF` names the reference for the system voltage angle; `SLACK` balances the system active and reactive mismatch and sets the reference angle; `ISOLATED` marks a bus not connected to the network.
ACBusType.title: ACBusType

AverageRateCurve.description: A curve whose y values are the average rate `f(x)/x` at production level `x` — total cost or fuel divided by output, the form heat rate tables use when they report MBTU/MWh against MW. `initial_input` records the total input at the minimum production point and is what makes conversion to an `InputOutputCurve` possible. Use `IncrementalCurve` when the data gives marginal rather than average rates.
AverageRateCurve.title: AverageRateCurve

ComplexNumber.description: A complex number, given as its `real` and `imag` parts.
ComplexNumber.title: ComplexNumber

CostCurve.description: Variable operation cost of a device expressed directly in currency. Wraps a `ValueCurve` that may be in input-output, incremental, or average-rate form, with `power_units` declaring the basis of the x axis and `vom_cost` adding a proportional variable operation and maintenance term.
CostCurve.title: CostCurve

DbdPnts.description: A pair of deadband thresholds `(dbd1, dbd2)` on a voltage or reactive-power error signal, inside which the controller does not act.
DbdPnts.title: DbdPnts

EmissionBasis.description: What an emission rate is measured against: `FUEL_INPUT` for mass per unit of heat input, `POWER_OUTPUT` for mass per unit of electrical output. The choice constrains the accompanying energy unit — a heat unit for `FUEL_INPUT`, `MWH` for `POWER_OUTPUT`.
EmissionBasis.title: EmissionBasis

EnergyUnit.description: Energy unit forming the denominator of an emission rate: `MMBTU` or `GJ` for a fuel-input basis, `MWH` for a power-output basis.
EnergyUnit.title: EnergyUnit

EnergyUnitBasis.description: Unit basis a stored-energy quantity is recorded in (distinct from EnergyUnit, which names fuel energy content). MWH: megawatt-hours, the conventional interchange form. MWMIN: megawatt-minutes, consistent with the minutes basis used for operational durations, so a duration computed as energy over power comes out in minutes with no hidden factor of 60. Defaults to MWH: MWMIN is supported, not preferred.
EnergyUnitBasis.title: EnergyUnitBasis

FdbdPnts.description: A pair of deadband thresholds `(fdbd1, fdbd2)` on a frequency error signal, inside which the controller does not act.
FdbdPnts.title: FdbdPnts

FromTo.description: A pair of values, one at the `from` end and one at the `to` end of a directed edge.
FromTo.title: FromTo

FromTo_ToFrom.description: A pair of values for a directed edge, one for each orientation: `from_to` and `to_from`. The two are carried separately because the quantity need not be equal in the two directions.
FromTo_ToFrom.title: FromTo_ToFrom

FuelCurve.description: Variable operation cost of a device expressed in fuel consumed — MBTU, liters, m^3 — together with the price that converts fuel to currency. Wraps a `ValueCurve` in input-output, incremental, or average-rate form; exactly one of `fuel_cost` and `fuel_cost_time_series` supplies the price.

fuel_cost.description: Fixed fuel cost per unit of fuel, or null when fuel_cost_time_series names a time-varying one. Exactly one of the two is set; producers and consumers enforce it.

fuel_cost_time_series.description: Store-minted id of the fuel-cost time series association, or null when fuel_cost carries a fixed value. Exactly one of the two is set.

startup_fuel_offtake.description: Fuel consumed during startup, as a curve in the unit's fuel units.

FuelCurve.title: FuelCurve

FunctionData.description: Raw mathematical data defining a function `f(x)` — coefficients or point tables with no units or interpretation attached. `function_type` selects the shape: linear, quadratic, piecewise linear through (x, y) points, or piecewise constant between x endpoints. What `x` and `y` stand for is supplied by whatever wraps this, and the `TIME_SERIES_*` variants hold a reference to a stored series in place of the numbers.
FunctionData.title: FunctionData

GenericOperationCost.description: Operating cost of a generation technology, selected by `cost_type` among the thermal (`THERMAL`), renewable (`RENEWABLE`), and hydro (`HYDRO_GEN`) generation cost representations.
GenericOperationCost.title: GenericOperationCost

HydroGenerationCost.description: Cost representation for hydro gen units
HydroGenerationCost.title: HydroGenerationCost

HydroStorageGenerationCost.description: Operating cost of hydro generation with storage, selected by `cost_type` between the hydro generation (`HYDRO_GEN`) and storage (`STORAGE`) cost representations.
HydroStorageGenerationCost.title: HydroStorageGenerationCost

ImpedanceUnitBasis.description: Unit basis a branch/injection impedance is stored in. NATURAL_UNITS: physical ohms (PSS/E RAW native for DC-line impedances). COMPONENT_BASE: per-unit on the component's own base (base_power MVA and voltage base); components whose per-unit data was historically on the system base record that system base in base_power, so there is no separate system-base option. PSS/E supplies device base for DC-line converters and CZ=2 transformer windings. A branch's shunt admittance halves (b, g) share the branch's one basis: NATURAL_UNITS stores them in siemens.
ImpedanceUnitBasis.title: ImpedanceUnitBasis

AdmittanceUnitBasis.description: Unit basis a shunt admittance is stored in. NATURAL_UNITS: physical siemens. COMPONENT_MVAR: reactive power at unity voltage (Mvar for susceptance, MW for conductance). COMPONENT_BASE: per-unit on the component's own base (base_power MVA and voltage base) — a per-unit base, not a power at unity voltage, and not an alternative spelling of COMPONENT_MVAR; components whose per-unit data was historically on the system base record that system base in base_power. Fixed and switched shunts use ShuntAdmittanceUnitBasis instead, which omits COMPONENT_BASE because a shunt has no device MVA rating.
AdmittanceUnitBasis.title: AdmittanceUnitBasis

ShuntAdmittanceUnitBasis.description: Subset of AdmittanceUnitBasis for fixed and switched shunts: omits COMPONENT_BASE because a shunt has no device MVA rating to per-unitize against. NATURAL_UNITS: physical siemens. COMPONENT_MVAR: reactive power at unity voltage (Mvar for susceptance, MW for conductance) — PSS/E RAW native for shunts.
ShuntAdmittanceUnitBasis.title: ShuntAdmittanceUnitBasis

ImportExportCost.description: Cost representation for static (non-time-varying) imports and exports with neighboring areas, together with the ancillary services offered alongside them. The offer curves are piecewise incremental cost curves with an implied zero cost at zero power, and a weekly energy limit bounds each direction. The time-varying counterpart is `ImportExportTimeSeriesCost`.

energy_import_weekly_limit.description: Weekly limit on imported energy, in MWh. MWh is the only representation: neither producers nor consumers rescale it by a system base. Units: MWh.

energy_export_weekly_limit.description: Weekly limit on exported energy, in MWh. MWh is the only representation: neither producers nor consumers rescale it by a system base. Units: MWh.

ImportExportCost.title: ImportExportCost

ImportExportTimeSeriesCost.description: Cost representation for time-varying imports and exports with neighboring areas. The static counterpart is ImportExportCost.

import_offer_curves.description: Import price curves whose value curve admits only the TIME_SERIES_INCREMENTAL variant; any other variant is rejected by the consuming constructor.

export_offer_curves.description: Export price curves whose value curve admits only the TIME_SERIES_INCREMENTAL variant; any other variant is rejected by the consuming constructor.

energy_import_weekly_limit.description: Weekly limit on imported energy, in MWh. MWh is the only representation: neither producers nor consumers rescale it by a system base. Units: MWh.

energy_export_weekly_limit.description: Weekly limit on exported energy, in MWh. MWh is the only representation: neither producers nor consumers rescale it by a system base. Units: MWh.

ImportExportTimeSeriesCost.title: ImportExportTimeSeriesCost

IncrementalCurve.description: A curve whose y values are the marginal rate `f'(x)` at production level `x` — the native form for market bid stacks and incremental heat rate data. `initial_input` records the total input at the minimum production point, anchoring the absolute level and enabling conversion to an `InputOutputCurve`. Use `InputOutputCurve` when the data gives total cost at each output level.
IncrementalCurve.title: IncrementalCurve

InOut.description: A pair of values, one for the inbound (`in`) and one for the outbound (`out`) direction of a quantity.
InOut.title: InOut

InputOutputCurve.description: A curve whose y values are the total input `f(x)` at production level `x` — currency per hour against MW in a cost curve, fuel per hour against MW in a fuel curve. The y axis is an absolute quantity, not a rate; use `IncrementalCurve` for marginal-rate data.
InputOutputCurve.title: InputOutputCurve

LinearFunctionData.description: Data for a linear function `f(x) = proportional_term * x + constant_term`.
LinearFunctionData.title: LinearFunctionData

LoadCost.description: Cost representation for controllable load units
LoadCost.title: LoadCost

MassUnit.description: Mass unit an emission quantity is reported in: kilograms, pounds, short tons (2000 lb), or metric tons (1000 kg).
MassUnit.title: MassUnit

MarketBidCost.description: Cost representation for static (non-time-varying) market bids of energy and ancillary services.

minimum_energy_offer.description: Minimum-energy offer: cost to operate at minimum stable level, in $/MWh at the curve's minimum power, stored as submitted. $/h sources convert at parse (MEO = no-load cost / P_min). Legacy scalar promotion: a bare scalar value `s` from a legacy source converts to an `InputOutputCurve` of `LinearFunctionData` with `constant_term = s` and `proportional_term = 0`.

start_up.description: Start-up cost at different stages of the thermal cycle (hot, warm, cold).

shut_down.description: Shut-down cost. Legacy scalar promotion: a bare scalar value `s` from a legacy source converts to an `InputOutputCurve` of `LinearFunctionData` with `constant_term = s` and `proportional_term = 0`.

incremental_offer_curves.description: Sell offer curves data as a `CostCurve` of `PiecewiseIncrementalCurve`.

decremental_offer_curves.description: Buy offer curves data as a `CostCurve` of `PiecewiseIncrementalCurve`.

ancillary_service_offers.description: IDs of the ancillary service components that this market bid offers into.

incremental_slope.description: Linear-interpolation flag for the incremental offer curves; false (default) is the step interpretation. Mutually exclusive with block groups on the same curve.

decremental_slope.description: Linear-interpolation flag for the decremental offer curves; false (default) is the step interpretation. Mutually exclusive with block groups on the same curve.

curve_style.description: Curve-clearing style for the bid: 0 = CURVE (ordinary divisible price-setting curve, default); 1 = FIXED (clears as one indivisible all-or-nothing package over its period); 2 = VARIABLE (divisible quantity, block-priced, cannot set the settlement-point price). A non-zero value is mutually exclusive with incremental_slope/decremental_slope.

curve_multihour.description: Multi-hour block indicator for the bid: 0 = SINGLE_HOUR (default; each hour of the bid clears independently); 1 = MULTI_HOUR (the bid must be awarded as one block across every hour it covers). Independent of curve_style: curve_style is the quantity structure, curve_multihour is the time structure, and they compose.

MarketBidCost.title: MarketBidCost

MarketBidTimeSeriesCost.description: Cost representation for time-varying market bids of energy and ancillary services. The static counterpart is MarketBidCost.

minimum_energy_offer.description: Minimum-energy offer: cost to operate at minimum stable level, in $/MWh at the curve's minimum power, stored as submitted. $/h sources convert at parse (MEO = no-load cost / P_min). Time-series-backed linear curve; only the TIME_SERIES_LINEAR function-data variant is admissible here — the consuming constructor rejects any other.

start_up_association_id.description: Store-minted id of a time series of three-stage (hot, warm, cold) start-up costs.

shut_down.description: Shut-down cost as a time-series-backed linear curve. Only the TIME_SERIES_LINEAR function-data variant is admissible here; the consuming constructor rejects any other.

incremental_offer_curves.description: Sell offer curves whose value curve is a time-series-backed piecewise incremental curve. Only the TIME_SERIES_INCREMENTAL variant is admissible here; any other variant is rejected by the consuming constructor.

decremental_offer_curves.description: Buy offer curves whose value curve is a time-series-backed piecewise incremental curve. Only the TIME_SERIES_INCREMENTAL variant is admissible here; any other variant is rejected by the consuming constructor.

ancillary_service_offers.description: IDs of the ancillary service components that this bid offers into.

incremental_slope.description: Linear-interpolation flag for the incremental offer curves; false (default) is the step interpretation. Mutually exclusive with block groups on the same curve.

decremental_slope.description: Linear-interpolation flag for the decremental offer curves; false (default) is the step interpretation. Mutually exclusive with block groups on the same curve.

curve_style.description: Curve-clearing style for the bid: 0 = CURVE (ordinary divisible price-setting curve, default); 1 = FIXED (clears as one indivisible all-or-nothing package over its period); 2 = VARIABLE (divisible quantity, block-priced, cannot set the settlement-point price). A non-zero value is mutually exclusive with incremental_slope/decremental_slope.

curve_multihour.description: Multi-hour block indicator for the bid: 0 = SINGLE_HOUR (default; each hour of the bid clears independently); 1 = MULTI_HOUR (the bid must be awarded as one block across every hour it covers). Independent of curve_style: curve_style is the quantity structure, curve_multihour is the time structure, and they compose.

MarketBidTimeSeriesCost.title: MarketBidTimeSeriesCost

MinMax.description: A pair of values bounding a quantity from below (`min`) and from above (`max`).
MinMax.title: MinMax

PiecewiseLinearData.description: Data for a piecewise linear function defined by (x, y) points and interpolated linearly between consecutive ones. The y values are absolute values at each x, not per-segment slopes; use `PiecewiseStepData` when the data gives per-segment rates. Points run in ascending x order, and two of them define one segment.
PiecewiseLinearData.title: PiecewiseLinearData

PiecewiseStepData.description: Data for a step function, constant on each segment, defined by the x coordinates of the segment endpoints and one y value per segment. The y values are per-segment rates, not absolute values; use `PiecewiseLinearData` when the data gives a value at each point. `x_coords` ascends and holds at least two entries, and `y_coords` holds exactly one fewer.
PiecewiseStepData.title: PiecewiseStepData

PollutantType.description: Pollutant an emission rate is reported for, spanning greenhouse gases (`CO2`, `CO2E`, `CH4`, `N2O`), criteria pollutants (`NOX`, `SO2`, `CO`, `VOC`, `PM25`, `PM10`), and toxics (`HG`, `HAP`), with `CUSTOM` for a user-defined pollutant.
PollutantType.title: PollutantType

PrimeMovers.description: Prime mover of a generating unit — the engine, turbine, water wheel, or similar machine that drives the generator — using the code set from the EIA Form 923 instructions. `PVe` is photovoltaic, spelled that way so it does not collide with the `PV` bus type.
PrimeMovers.title: PrimeMovers

ProductionVariableCostCurve.description: Variable production cost of a device, selected by `variable_cost_type` between a curve denominated directly in currency (`COST`) and one denominated in fuel with a separate fuel price (`FUEL`).
ProductionVariableCostCurve.title: ProductionVariableCostCurve

QuadraticFunctionData.description: Data for a quadratic function `f(x) = quadratic_term * x^2 + proportional_term * x + constant_term`. A non-negative `quadratic_term` makes the function convex.
QuadraticFunctionData.title: QuadraticFunctionData

RenewableGenerationCost.description: Cost representation for renewable generation units
RenewableGenerationCost.title: RenewableGenerationCost

ReservoirLocation.description: Position of a hydro reservoir relative to its turbine: `HEAD` upstream of the turbine, typically at higher elevation; `TAIL` downstream, at lower or equal elevation.
ReservoirLocation.title: ReservoirLocation

StartUpShutDown.description: A pair of values, one for the start-up phase and one for the shut-down phase of a unit's cycle.
StartUpShutDown.title: StartUpShutDown

StartUpStages.description: A triple of values, one for each stage of a thermal unit's start-up: `hot`, `warm`, and `cold`.
StartUpStages.title: StartUpStages

StorageTech.description: defines the storage technology used in an energy Storage system, based on the options in EIA form 923.
StorageTech.title: StorageTech

ThermalFuels.description: Thermal fuels that reflect options in the EIA annual energy review.
ThermalFuels.title: ThermalFuels

ThermalGenerationCost.title: ThermalGenerationCost
ThermalGenerationCost.description: Cost representation for thermal generation units

fixed.description: Fixed cost of keeping the unit online. For some cost represenations this field can be duplicative

shut_down.description: Cost to turn the unit off

start_up.description: Start-up cost can take linear or multi-stage cost

function_data.description: Only TIME_SERIES_LINEAR or TIME_SERIES_PIECEWISE_STEP is admissible here; all other FunctionData variants, static or time-series-backed, are rejected by the consuming constructor.

initial_input_association_id.description: Store-minted id of the time series supplying the initial input value, or null.

input_at_zero_association_id.description: Store-minted id of the time series supplying the input at zero output, or null.

TimeSeriesAverageRateCurve.title: TimeSeriesAverageRateCurve
TimeSeriesAverageRateCurve.description: A time-series-backed average rate curve. The static counterpart is AverageRateCurve.

function_data.description: Only TIME_SERIES_LINEAR or TIME_SERIES_PIECEWISE_STEP is admissible here; all other FunctionData variants, static or time-series-backed, are rejected by the consuming constructor.

initial_input_association_id.description: Store-minted id of the time series supplying the initial input value, or null.

input_at_zero_association_id.description: Store-minted id of the time series supplying the input at zero output, or null.

TimeSeriesIncrementalCurve.title: TimeSeriesIncrementalCurve
TimeSeriesIncrementalCurve.description: A time-series-backed incremental curve. The static counterpart is IncrementalCurve.

function_data.description: Only TIME_SERIES_LINEAR, TIME_SERIES_QUADRATIC, or TIME_SERIES_PIECEWISE_LINEAR is admissible here; the static variants and TIME_SERIES_PIECEWISE_STEP are invalid and rejected by the consuming constructor.

input_at_zero.description: Optional explicit input value at zero output. A number here, unlike the incremental and average-rate variants, where it is a time series reference.

TimeSeriesInputOutputCurve.title: TimeSeriesInputOutputCurve
TimeSeriesInputOutputCurve.description: A time-series-backed input-output curve. The static counterpart is InputOutputCurve.

TimeSeriesLinearFunctionData.description: Time-series-backed variant of `LinearFunctionData`. In place of inline coefficients it carries `association_id`, referencing a stored series that supplies them at each step; use it when the coefficients change over time.

association_id.description: Store-minted id of the time series association whose values supply this function data over time. Resolved against the accompanying time series store on read; minted by that store and meaningful only against it, never assigned by a document producer.

TimeSeriesLinearFunctionData.title: TimeSeriesLinearFunctionData

TimeSeriesPiecewiseLinearData.description: Time-series-backed variant of `PiecewiseLinearData`. In place of an inline point table it carries `association_id`, referencing a stored series that supplies one at each step; use it when the points change over time.

association_id.description: Store-minted id of the time series association whose values supply this function data over time. Resolved against the accompanying time series store on read; minted by that store and meaningful only against it, never assigned by a document producer.

TimeSeriesPiecewiseLinearData.title: TimeSeriesPiecewiseLinearData

TimeSeriesPiecewiseStepData.description: Time-series-backed variant of `PiecewiseStepData`. In place of inline coordinate vectors it carries `association_id`, referencing a stored series that supplies them at each step; use it when the segments change over time.

association_id.description: Store-minted id of the time series association whose values supply this function data over time. Resolved against the accompanying time series store on read; minted by that store and meaningful only against it, never assigned by a document producer.

TimeSeriesPiecewiseStepData.title: TimeSeriesPiecewiseStepData

TimeSeriesQuadraticFunctionData.description: Time-series-backed variant of `QuadraticFunctionData`. In place of inline coefficients it carries `association_id`, referencing a stored series that supplies them at each step; use it when the coefficients change over time.

association_id.description: Store-minted id of the time series association whose values supply this function data over time. Resolved against the accompanying time series store on read; minted by that store and meaningful only against it, never assigned by a document producer.

TimeSeriesQuadraticFunctionData.title: TimeSeriesQuadraticFunctionData

TurbinePump.description: A pair of values, one for the turbine (generating) mode and one for the pump (charging) mode of a pumped hydro unit.
TurbinePump.title: TurbinePump

TwoTerminalLoss.description: Loss model of a two-terminal HVDC line as a function of flow, selected by `curve_type`. It accepts a linear model with a constant loss and a proportional loss rate (MW of loss per MW of flow), or a piecewise model giving different proportional losses on different flow segments.
TwoTerminalLoss.title: TwoTerminalLoss

UnitSystem.description: Unit basis a stored value is expressed in. COMPONENT_BASE: per-unit against a base the component records itself. NATURAL_UNITS: the quantity's own physical unit. No system-wide option: a value per-unitized against a shared base records that base on the component and rides as COMPONENT_BASE. Used in three scopes, each read against its own record rather than a document-wide table: a component's own `power_units` (against that component's `base_power`), a cost payload's own `power_units` (e.g. `CostCurve`, against the owning component's `base_power`), and a time series association's own `unit_system` (governing only that one series).
UnitSystem.title: UnitSystem

UpDown.description: A pair of values, one for the upward (`up`) and one for the downward (`down`) direction of a quantity.
UpDown.title: UpDown

ValueCurve.description: A cost or fuel curve: function data plus a declaration of how to read its y axis. `INPUT_OUTPUT` reads y as the total `f(x)`, `INCREMENTAL` as the marginal rate `f'(x)`, and `AVERAGE_RATE` as the average `f(x)/x`; the three can express the same underlying function and are inter-convertible given `initial_input`. The `TIME_SERIES_*` variants are the time-varying equivalents. Which form to use follows the data source: bid stacks are incremental, total cost tables input-output, efficiency tables average rate.
ValueCurve.title: ValueCurve

XY_Coords.description: A single point, given as its `x` and `y` coordinates.
XY_Coords.title: XY_Coords
